claims.text: Surface defects and microstructural inhomogeneities in the damaged component predispose it to hot cracking under high-temperature corrosive conditions.
Traditional fusion-welding repair is prone to hot cracking in the target component.
Laser cladding can produce crack-free AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and Y/Hf-co-doped AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA coatings.
The as-deposited AlCoCrFeNi2.1-based coatings contain FCC and BCC/B2 phases.
Heat treatment produces an Al-rich L12 precipitate within the FCC phase.
Y and Hf co-doping improves the thermal stability of the EHEA coating.
Y and Hf co-doping improves the adhesion and stability of protective oxide scales.
Y and Hf co-doping improves resistance to hot-corrosion oxide-scale spallation.
Shot peening can change the surface residual stress of a laser-cladded repair from tensile to compressive.
Shot-peening-induced compressive residual stress reduces surface tensile-stress concentrations and forming defects.
A refined and thermally stable EHEA microstructure resists crack initiation.
The proposed laser-cladded, optionally shot-peened repair will delay hot-crack initiation.
The proposed repair will reduce hot-corrosion scale spallation relative to traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser-directed energy deposition combined with shot peening can produce a finer repaired microstructure.
The mechanical properties of the repaired region can approach those of the base material.
A service environment of 900 °C with 75% Na2SO4 and 25% NaCl is an applicable hot-corrosion test condition for the EHEA coatings.
Optimized laser-cladding parameters can avoid additional thermal damage to the target component.
The method is effective primarily for superficial damage that can be repaired by coating deposition.
Extreme component geometries or extensive damage may reduce the benefit of the repair.

contradictions.description: Shot peening is described as optional, but the hypothesized mediator and mechanism rely on shot-peening-induced compressive residual stress. The experiment also leaves peening optional rather than separating peened and unpeened laser-clad groups, making that causal contribution ambiguous.
